h1: The 7 Best Monitor Arms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven monitor arms from gas spring Ergotron models to budget clamp mounts, with weight limits, VESA support and screen sizes.
summary: The Ergotron LX is the best monitor arm, a gas spring design for screens up to 34 inches and 7 to 25 lb. The HUANUO TitanLift holds up to 44 lb and screens up to 49 inches for $50 to $100, and the Ergotron LX Pro suits lighter screens at 4 to 22 lb in white. The FlowLift and FlowLift Pro, WALI and ErGear are budget arms, with the WALI holding 26.4 lb.
intro: A monitor arm fails slowly. It holds the screen on day one, then the display creeps downward over a week because the weight was outside the arm's window. That capacity range is not a ceiling you can lean on. Both ends matter: a screen too light makes a gas spring pop upward, and one too heavy sags, and the spec sheet is the only place that warns you.

We reviewed eight arms and ranked seven, scoring them on the Primea framework with screen size, weight range, VESA pattern, mechanism and mounting weighted most. Prices appear as buckets. Find your monitor's weight and VESA pattern before you start, because those two numbers eliminate most of the field, and they take a minute to check.

products.name: Ergotron LX Monitor Arm
products.verdict: The proven gas spring arm for standard and ultrawide screens.
products.description:
The Ergotron LX uses a gas spring for height and depth adjustment and supports flat, curved and ultrawide monitors up to 34 inches. It carries 7 to 25 pounds and fits VESA 75x75mm or 100x100mm in matte black, in the $100 to $200 bucket. Gas springs balance the screen's weight, so it floats where you leave it instead of needing a tightened knob.

It ranks first because its capacity range is wider than the budget FlowLift's and its motion is proven, while the TitanLift covers heavier panels but with a less refined feel. The LX Pro lowers the minimum weight but also the maximum.

Buy it for most desks with a 21 to 34 inch monitor. The caveat is the 7 lb minimum load: skip it if your screen weighs under 7 pounds, because the spring will push it up.
products.idealFor: Most desks with a 21 to 34 inch monitor.

products.name: HUANUO TitanLift Heavy Duty Monitor Arm
products.verdict: Holds up to 44 pounds and screens up to 49 inches.
products.description:
The TitanLift is an aluminum arm for screens up to 49 inches carrying up to 44 pounds, with a dual C-clamp base and a maximum VESA of 100x100mm, in the $50 to $100 bucket. A dual clamp spreads the load across two points, which helps when a big super-ultrawide pulls on the arm.

It ranks second because it handles displays the Ergotron cannot, 49 inches and 44 lb against 34 inches and 25 lb, and it does so at about half the price. It gives up the refined feel of the Ergotron.

Buy it for large ultrawide and curved monitors. The caveats are the 100x100mm VESA ceiling and a less polished brand. Skip it if you use a small, light monitor, because a 44 lb arm is overbuilt and its spring may be too strong.
products.skipIf: You use a small, light monitor.

products.name: Ergotron LX Pro Premium Monitor Arm
products.verdict: A white finish and upgraded spring for long-term use.
products.description:
The Ergotron LX Pro adds an upgraded gas spring mechanism and a white finish, supporting monitors up to 34 inches from 4 to 22 pounds on VESA 75x75mm or 100x100mm. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket. The lower 4 lb floor suits lightweight displays that the standard LX would push upward.

It ranks below the standard LX because its heavy end is lower at 22 pounds, though it handles lighter screens from 4 pounds. It stays ahead of the HUANUO arms thanks to the spring upgrade and the finish.

Buy it for light monitors on a white desk, where the matching color makes a visible difference. The caveat is the 22 lb ceiling, so skip it if your screen exceeds that, and note that it costs the same as the standard LX.
products.idealFor: Light monitors on a white desk.

products.name: HUANUO FlowLift Single Monitor Mount
products.verdict: Clamp and grommet bases in the box for a low price.
products.description:
The FlowLift fits 13 to 32 inch monitors weighing 4.4 to 19.8 pounds, with a clamp and a grommet base both included. It offers tilt, swivel and rotation, in the $25 to $50 bucket. Having both bases in the box means you can choose the install that suits your desk, without buying a second kit.

It ranks fourth because the capacity is lower than the Ergotron and the build is more modest. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket, which is a bargain next to the $100 to $200 arms.

Buy it for standard monitors on a budget. The caveats are the 32 inch limit and the 19.8 lb ceiling, so skip it if you own an ultrawide or a heavy display, where the TitanLift or Ergotron fit properly.

products.name: HUANUO FlowLift Pro Monitor Arm
products.verdict: A tool-free VESA mount for 20 to 27 inch screens.
products.description:
The FlowLift Pro offers a tool-free VESA mount, a C-clamp and grommet base, and a 19.8 pound limit for 13 to 32 inch screens. Tilt, swivel and rotation are included, in the $25 to $50 bucket. A tool-free mount lets you hang the monitor without hunting for a screwdriver.

It ranks fifth because it matches the plain FlowLift on capacity, with the tool-free mount as its main addition. It sits behind the plain FlowLift only on listing detail, not on function, so the gap is small.

Buy it for quick installs on mid-size monitors. The caveats are the same weight cap and no ultrawide support. Skip it if you want a heavier capacity, because the WALI holds more for less money.

products.name: WALI Single Monitor Mount
products.verdict: Holds 26.4 pounds, more than any other budget arm here.
products.description:
The WALI supports 13 to 34 inch screens, with a regular screen limit of 32 inches, and holds up to 26.4 pounds. It takes VESA 75 or 100mm and comes in black, in the under $25 bucket. Holding 26.4 lb beats every other budget arm here, and even edges the Ergotron LX's 25 lb ceiling on paper.

It ranks sixth because the listing is sparse on the clamp and mechanism, even though the capacity beats the FlowLift. A high number on a cheap arm tells you less than the same number from a brand that documents the spring.

Buy it for a heavier monitor on a tight budget. The caveat is sparse detail, so skip it if you want a polished mechanism, and expect to adjust tension by hand.
products.idealFor: Heavier monitors on a tight budget.

products.name: ErGear Single Monitor Arm
products.verdict: A tool-free arm with cable management at the lowest price.
products.description:
The ErGear fits 13 to 34 inch screens, holds 19.8 pounds and uses a tool-free VESA mount up to 100x100mm. Built-in cable management keeps wires tidy. It sits in the under $25 bucket. Cable channels in the arm hide the cords that otherwise dangle behind a floating screen.

It ranks last because its capacity is lower than the WALI, though it matches the FlowLift models. The 34 inch fit is a plus, since few budget arms list it.

Buy it as a first arm for a modest monitor. The caveats are the 19.8 lb ceiling and a basic build, so skip it if you have a heavy display. Everything else here either carries more or adds a better mechanism.

whatMatters.detail: Every arm has a minimum and maximum load. A screen too light makes the arm spring upward, while one too heavy makes it sag. Find your monitor's weight on its spec sheet and compare it with the arm's range, such as 7 to 25 lb on the Ergotron LX, and leave margin on both ends. A screen near either limit will never sit quite right.

VESA is the hole layout on the back of your display, usually 75x75mm or 100x100mm. If it does not match, the arm will not attach. Check your monitor's manual or the back panel, and note that some displays have no VESA holes and need an adapter bracket sold separately. A mismatched pattern is the top reason arms get returned.

Arms are rated by diagonal size, but ultrawides are wider and heavier than their number suggests. A 34 inch ultrawide can outweigh a 32 inch flat screen. Check that your display falls inside the listed range for both size and weight, and for ultrawides prefer arms that name them, such as the Ergotron LX. A weight figure for the panel without its stand is what you want.

Gas springs allow smooth motion with minimal force, while mechanical springs are simpler and cheaper. This affects how easily you reposition the screen through the day. Look for the mechanism name in the title or specs, and expect budget arms to need more tension adjustment than the Ergotron models. Cheaper springs tend to loosen with use, so recheck tension each season.

Clamps grip the desk edge, and grommet mounts pass through a hole in the desk. Thick, glass or bare-edged desks may not suit a clamp. Measure your desk thickness and check the arm's clamp range, and choose a model like the FlowLift that includes both options if you are unsure. Standing desks and thick tops often need the grommet route.

faq.q: How do I know if a monitor arm fits my monitor?
faq.a: Match the VESA pattern and the weight. Both must fall inside the arm's listed range, such as 75x75 or 100x100mm and 7 to 25 lb on the Ergotron LX. Weigh your screen without the stand.

faq.q: Can I mount a monitor without VESA holes?
faq.a: Not directly. Some monitors need an adapter bracket, so check your model first. All arms here use VESA 75 or 100mm, so a monitor without those holes will not mount. Measure the hole spacing with a ruler if the manual is missing.

faq.q: Is a gas spring arm worth it?
faq.a: If you move the screen often, yes. For a fixed position, a basic arm like the FlowLift or WALI is fine. Ergotron's gas spring suits frequent adjustment, such as switching between sitting and standing positions.

faq.q: Will a clamp damage my desk?
faq.a: It can mark soft surfaces, so use a pad if your desk is delicate. A grommet mount, included with the FlowLift, avoids the clamp pressure on the edge.

faq.q: How do I fix a drooping arm?
faq.a: Adjust the tension screw, or check whether the monitor is too heavy for the arm. The LX Pro suits screens of 4 to 22 lb, while the WALI tops out at 26.4 lb. Overloaded arms droop first at the joint.

faq.q: Can one arm hold two monitors?
faq.a: Only if it is designed for it. These are all single monitor arms, so a second screen needs a second arm or a dual model. Plan desk space for two clamps.

finalTake: Buy the Ergotron LX for a standard or ultrawide screen up to 34 inches and 25 lb. Take the TitanLift if your display is bigger or heavier, and the LX Pro for light screens on a white desk. Budget buyers can choose the FlowLift for dual bases, the WALI for capacity, or the ErGear for the lowest price. Match weight and VESA before anything else.
